creator: opichillc
title: Anecdote: same task run in Claude Code terminal burned ~75% of a 5-hour usage limit and bloated the diff, while the VS Code extension used ~3-4% and changed ~15 lines; suspects terminal spawning unneeded sub-agents
claims: Over a few days, context consumption rose with no workflow change
Same instructions: terminal changed unneeded code and used ~75% of the 5-hour limit; VS Code panel changed ~15 lines and used ~3-4%
Hypothesis: terminal mode spins up extra sub-agents for simple tasks
how_to_steps: Run the identical prompt in the terminal and in the VS Code extension
Compare lines changed and usage-limit consumption
on_screen_only: 'Is Claude Code using up all your tokens?' header; captions only
cta: Comment if you have seen the same

relevance.why: Token burn matters to a time- and budget-constrained founder, but this is a single uncontrolled comparison with no numbers from /cost; most likely confounded by effort/auto-mode settings or session context size.

implement_score.why: Worth a 10-minute self-check (/cost and /doctor on a simple task in each surface) before believing it; no action otherwise.

verify: Were effort level, model, permission mode and loaded skills identical in both surfaces?
Did the terminal session carry a large prior context?
Is there any known difference in sub-agent behaviour between CLI and extension?

gap.what: A warning (not a technique) that surface choice may change token burn; liked set had /doctor and token-saving skills but no CLI-vs-extension comparison. Weak evidence.
